# lockrot

> lockrot finds abandoned, unmaintained and branch-pinned packages in a PHP project's composer.lock, and releases that promise a PHP version they were never tested against. It is a Composer plugin and a standalone PHAR, MIT-licensed, for PHP 7.4+ and Composer 2.2+. It reads composer.json and composer.lock and writes to neither.

`composer audit --abandoned` reads one field, the `abandoned` marker a maintainer sets by hand on Packagist. lockrot reads that field too, then checks when the last stable release landed, when the repository was last pushed to, whether the lock file holds a branch snapshot instead of a version, whether a release older than the target PHP's major has an open-ended `require.php`, and whether a release's `require.php` stops below the newest PHP the project allows. Every finding carries its flags with their evidence, a score with the sum behind it, and the chain of requirements that pulled the package in. The score's band is the grade. The security advisories `composer audit` would report add to the score.

Install: `composer require --dev somework/lockrot`, or download https://lockrot.dev/lockrot.phar. Run: `composer lockrot --target-php=8.4`. In CI: `--fail-on` takes a comma-separated list, at most one grade, one flag, one `vulnerable` severity and `unchecked`; exit 0 is clean, 1 means a finding failed a value or `--strict-network` tripped, 2 is lockrot's own error.

## Reference

- [What it reports](https://lockrot.dev/verdicts/): the eight flags (abandoned, silent, pinned, left-behind, old-promise, stale, capped, vulnerable), the signals behind them, the score that adds them up and the verdict. The verdict is a grade (critical, high, medium, low), or unknown, finished or ok at score 0. The flags are the facts. `lead` is the 0.13 word, or `capped`, which 0.13 did not have, and null when only vulnerable counts. Each finding prints the sum behind its score. Also why an advisory with no reachable fix counts twice, and the move that each graded finding's `do:` line names
- [Score model 1](https://lockrot.dev/verdicts/model-1/): the rules that grade a finding in lockrot 0.14.0 and later, in the order they apply, each with its parameters and an example; every report-2 links its rules here
- [Configuration](https://lockrot.dev/configuration/): every `extra.lockrot` key, environment overrides, CLI options, caching, the allowlist, and `--explain=vendor/package` (from 0.8.0), which prints why one package got its verdict: every signal's raw data, the repository's release branches with their dates, the thresholds
- [In CI](https://lockrot.dev/ci/): the GitHub Action, exit codes, and the github, sarif, gitlab, markdown and json formats
- [Reading a report](https://lockrot.dev/viewer/): what a report says, how its flags add up to a score and a grade, and the viewer at https://viewer.lockrot.dev/ that opens one in the browser
- [Baseline](https://lockrot.dev/baseline/): accept today's findings, fail only on new and worsened ones
- [JSON schemas](https://lockrot.dev/schema/): the published draft-04 schemas for the report, the explanation, the baseline file and `extra.lockrot` (from 0.9.0), what they type, the rule behind their version numbers, and how to validate a report in CI
- [Report schema 1](https://lockrot.dev/schema/report-1/): the field tables of report-1, the report of lockrot 0.13 and older, frozen from lockrot v0.13.0
- [Report schema 2](https://lockrot.dev/schema/report-2/): the field tables of report-2, the report of lockrot 0.14.0 and later. In report-2 the verdict is a grade. The flags are the facts. `lead` is the 0.13 word, or `capped`, which 0.13 did not have, and null when only vulnerable counts. The sum is printed
- [Run notes](https://lockrot.dev/notes/): every note a run can carry, looked up by its code: what the run could not see, whether it fails `--strict-network`, its effect on findings, its typed data and what to do about it
- [Compatibility](https://lockrot.dev/compatibility/): the draft of the 1.0 promise: which JSON fields, closed and open sets, exit codes, options and configuration keys stay stable, how a release may change a verdict, the names reserved for extensions, and how a deprecation is announced
- [Install-time summary](https://lockrot.dev/install-time/): what the plugin prints during composer require, update and install
- [PHAR and self-update](https://lockrot.dev/phar/): verified download, GPG signature, build provenance, PHIVE, Docker image, self-update
- [Data sources](https://lockrot.dev/internals/): Composer repositories, the GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket APIs, rate caps, credentials, caching, --offline

## Examples

- [Example run](https://lockrot.dev/example-run/): a complete report on a public 200-package composer.lock, as a table and as JSON

## Data

- [Weekly watch](https://lockrot.dev/watch/): every Monday lockrot's newest release reads two kinds of composer.lock — the one shipped by the newest stable release of widely used open-source PHP applications, and the one a project created that morning gets from composer create-project. Each row names the release tag and commit, or the starter package and version, links the full rendered report, and counts the flagged packages composer audit does not name at all; the reports of every earlier run stay published, and every run is kept in history.csv

## Blog

- [What composer audit --abandoned misses in 31 PHP projects](https://lockrot.dev/blog/2026/09/19/composer-audit-abandoned-misses/): 129 of 4,109 production packages in 31 open-source PHP applications are marked abandoned, archived or five years silent; composer audit --abandoned reports 62, because it reads the abandoned field from composer.lock rather than Packagist; data and lock-file commits linked
- [Blog index](https://lockrot.dev/blog/) and [RSS feed](https://lockrot.dev/feed_rss_created.xml)

## Optional

- [Upgrading to 0.14](https://lockrot.dev/changes/0.14/): what to do when lockrot 0.14 reaches a project: regenerate the baseline, change jq queries, or stay on 0.13 with the PHAR, the plugin, the action, Docker or PHIVE
- [Changelog](https://lockrot.dev/changelog/): what changed, release by release
